decisions.plan: Move toward grip x=0.02, y=0.10 m while retaining height; then lower over the center of the cavity.

decisions.plan: Finish the final 20 mm inward alignment and begin a short descent, then inspect wall clearance before lowering farther.
decisions.belief: The bowl is nearly centered above the bottom drawer cavity, with visible side clearance. The grasp and upright orientation remain stable.
decisions.why: Moves from transfer into placement while keeping the bowl inside the cavity footprint.

decisions.plan: Stop advancing inward and lower vertically in a short segment at the current horizontal alignment, monitoring cabinet and rim clearance.

decisions.why: Avoids pushing the hand farther toward the cabinet while testing a clear vertical placement route.

decisions.plan: Continue straight down in a 25 mm segment, watching for support and wall contact before release.
decisions.belief: Vertical lowering is progressing normally, and the bowl remains upright within the drawer footprint. The hand has stopped pressing inward toward the cabinet.
decisions.why: Lowers the bowl into the bottom drawer along the confirmed vertical route.

decisions.plan: Continue vertically downward by 20 mm, then reassess support and clearance.
decisions.belief: The bowl is descending upright into the cavity and still follows the hand. Its base appears above the drawer floor; release would be premature.
decisions.why: Brings the bowl closer to stable support inside the drawer without inward pressure on the cabinet.

decisions.plan: Use a short 8 mm downward target to distinguish continued free descent from a stop, then release inside the drawer once safely supported or just above its floor.
decisions.belief: The bowl is inside the drawer footprint and close to its floor, but downward progress slowed in the last segment. Hand contact near the cabinet handle or bowl support may be limiting motion.
decisions.why: Checks near-support motion without forcing a longer descent against possible contact.

decisions.plan: Open the fingers at this placement pose, let the bowl settle inside the drawer, then withdraw and inspect its support before closing the drawer.
decisions.belief: The short downward test reached a stop with essentially no motion. The bowl is upright over the drawer floor and fully within its visible footprint; exact support contact is occluded.
decisions.why: Releases at the intended destination without forcing further downward contact.

decisions.plan: Withdraw upward and slightly outward, verify the bowl stays in place, then approach the bottom drawer handle to close it.
decisions.belief: The released bowl has moved down onto the drawer floor and appears upright inside the cavity. The fingers are reopening; stable support will be checked after withdrawal.
decisions.why: Clears the bowl and cabinet without lifting it, revealing its final supported pose.

decisions.plan: Move outside the drawer front, close the empty fingers, then lower to the bottom handle and push inward along positive y in monitored segments.
decisions.belief: The bowl stayed upright and stationary on the bottom drawer floor after the gripper withdrew, supporting successful placement. The drawer is still open; the nearby bottle remains undisturbed.
decisions.why: Transitions from bowl placement to drawer closing without recontacting the bowl.

decisions.plan: Move outward to approximately y=0.005 m while beginning a modest descent, then align closed fingertips with the handle height.
decisions.belief: The bowl remains upright inside the drawer. The empty gripper is above the bottom handle but still needs to move to its outside face before lowering.
decisions.why: Creates clearance outside the handle for a controlled positive-y push.

decisions.plan: Lower toward handle height while remaining on its negative-y side, then make a short inward contact move.
decisions.belief: The closed fingertips are outside the bottom drawer handle, and the bowl is safely resting inside. The handle appears near z=0.94–0.96 m.
decisions.why: Aligns the closed finger side with the handle for a horizontal push rather than pressing on its top.

decisions.plan: Complete the descent to z=0.945 m at y=0.008 m, then approach the handle horizontally.
decisions.belief: The empty fingers are nearly closed and descending outside the bottom handle. The bowl remains stationary in the open drawer.
decisions.why: Sets the finger side at handle height for a controlled closing push.

decisions.plan: Approach the handle with a short positive-y move, then continue pushing only as drawer motion is observed.
decisions.belief: The closed fingertip side is approximately aligned with the bottom handle height, on its outside face. The bowl remains inside the drawer.
decisions.why: Establishes closing contact gently and tests the drawer's sliding response.

decisions.plan: Push the bottom handle inward along positive y at constant height, checking drawer motion after each segment.
decisions.belief: The fingertips have reached the handle, and the drawer front shifted slightly inward while the bowl moved with it. The bowl remains upright.
decisions.why: Continues the observed closing slide with controlled horizontal contact.

decisions.plan: Continue pushing the handle in positive y at the same height, monitoring the remaining drawer opening.
decisions.belief: The bottom drawer slid inward about 20 mm with the push, and the bowl stayed upright on its floor. Closing contact is effective and clear of the bottle.
decisions.why: Reduces the drawer opening while preserving the placed bowl.

decisions.plan: Continue the positive-y handle push, then shorten moves as the drawer approaches the cabinet face.
decisions.belief: The drawer continues sliding inward smoothly and the bowl remains contained and upright. A visible opening remains.
decisions.why: Further closes the remaining gap while monitoring the placed bowl and hand clearance.

decisions.plan: Lower the closed hand slightly while keeping its fingertips outside the drawer front, to clear the upper handle and continue pushing the bottom handle.
decisions.belief: The drawer moved inward again, but motion slowed near the same y position where the hand previously encountered cabinet clearance. A substantial drawer gap remains, so this is not the closed stop.
decisions.why: Changes the hand clearance geometry rather than forcing farther inward against a possible upper-handle obstruction.

decisions.plan: Withdraw from contact, then rotate the gripper so its wide hand body spans across rather than along the drawer's sliding direction; resume pushing after realignment.
decisions.belief: The attempted lowering barely moved the hand, confirming a local obstruction rather than drawer closure. The bowl remains inside the partially open drawer.
decisions.why: Relieves the obstruction and creates a new hand-clearance strategy instead of forcing the same contact.

decisions.plan: Rotate the gripper in small yaw increments toward a quarter-turn while moving a little farther outward, then reapproach the handle with a narrower inward profile.
decisions.belief: Withdrawal succeeded and the drawer stayed partially closed with the bowl inside. The hand is free to change orientation outside the front.
decisions.why: Begins the clearance-changing reorientation away from the cabinet.

decisions.plan: Continue the quarter-turn reorientation in bounded increments before recontacting the handle.
decisions.belief: The empty hand is rotating freely outside the drawer. The bowl and drawer have remained stationary during withdrawal.
decisions.why: Reduces the hand body's inward reach toward the upper cabinet handle.

decisions.plan: Continue turning toward a crosswise hand orientation before resuming the closing push.
decisions.belief: The hand is clear of the handle and yaw rotation is progressing. The bowl remains supported inside the partially closed drawer.
decisions.why: Further narrows the hand's projection toward the cabinet handles.

decisions.plan: Continue the clearance reorientation, then return the fingertips to the lower handle.
decisions.belief: The hand continues rotating without moving the drawer or bowl. More yaw is needed to make its broad axis crosswise.
decisions.why: Increases clearance to the upper handles during the remaining closing travel.

decisions.plan: Continue toward the crosswise orientation, then realign with the bottom handle to complete closure.
decisions.belief: The hand is rotating freely outside the drawer; the bowl remains undisturbed inside.
decisions.why: Increases clearance between the broad hand body and upper cabinet handles.

decisions.plan: Continue reorientation toward a crosswise hand profile before resuming closure.
decisions.belief: The hand has turned about 30 degrees and remains clear; the bowl is still upright in the drawer.
decisions.why: Prepares to avoid the upper-handle obstruction encountered during the first push.

decisions.plan: Continue toward the crosswise orientation for the remaining handle push.
decisions.belief: The hand is free and now turned about 37 degrees; the drawer and bowl are unchanged.
decisions.why: Further reduces the inward projection of the wide hand body.

decisions.plan: Continue the reorientation before reapproaching the bottom handle.
decisions.belief: The hand is approximately halfway through the quarter-turn and remains clear of the cabinet and bottle.
decisions.why: Makes the hand's broad axis increasingly perpendicular to the drawer slide direction.

decisions.plan: Continue the crosswise reorientation, then lower back to the bottom handle's pushing height.
decisions.belief: The hand is now turned roughly 50 degrees, with no unintended contact. The placed bowl remains stable.
decisions.why: Improves upper-handle clearance for the remaining drawer travel.

decisions.plan: Use a slightly smaller yaw target and continue toward a crosswise orientation before resuming the push.
decisions.belief: The last target was rejected for exceeding the rotation bound by 0.002 rad; no commanded motion occurred. The bowl remains inside the drawer and the hand is clear.
decisions.why: Keeps the clearance-changing rotation within the allowed local bound.

decisions.plan: Continue toward the crosswise orientation, then reapproach the lower handle for the remaining closing travel.
decisions.belief: The hand has turned roughly 57 degrees and remains clear; the bowl is stable inside the drawer.
decisions.why: Improves hand-body clearance to the upper handles.

decisions.plan: Finish the crosswise orientation, then lower and approach the handle along positive y.
decisions.belief: The hand is turned about 64 degrees and remains clear. The bowl is stationary inside the drawer.
decisions.why: Prepares a narrower hand profile for the last portion of drawer closure.

decisions.plan: Continue toward the final crosswise orientation while lowering to the established handle pushing height.
decisions.belief: The hand is now nearly crosswise and remains outside the drawer front. The bowl remains supported inside.
decisions.why: Combines final clearance preparation with vertical realignment for resuming closure.

decisions.plan: Move toward the bottom handle while finishing the quarter-turn; inspect contact before pushing farther.
decisions.belief: The fingertips are back near handle height with the hand nearly crosswise. The drawer and bowl remain stationary during preparation.
decisions.why: Returns to closing contact with a substantially narrower inward hand profile.

decisions.plan: Approach the handle with a short inward move while settling the final yaw, then resume monitored pushing.
decisions.belief: The hand is nearly fully crosswise and aligned at the bottom handle height. The bowl remains in the drawer; handle contact is still just ahead.
decisions.why: Establishes closing contact with the new clearance profile.

decisions.plan: Resume a short inward push and inspect whether the drawer advances past the earlier obstruction point.
decisions.belief: The hand has reached the handle area in the crosswise orientation without the prior stall. The bowl remains upright inside the drawer.
decisions.why: Tests the improved-clearance closing approach before committing to longer pushes.

decisions.plan: Continue positive-y pushes at constant height, monitoring for the final closed position.
decisions.belief: The crosswise approach passed the former stall point, and the drawer has begun sliding inward again. The bowl remains contained.
decisions.why: Closes the remaining drawer travel with the corrected hand clearance.

decisions.plan: Back away slightly and tilt the hand so its body stays outward while the fingertips reach the bottom handle; preserve the bowl in the drawer.
decisions.belief: The drawer advanced farther but the hand is again close to an upper handle and inward motion slowed. The remaining visible opening means closure is unfinished.
decisions.why: Creates another clearance advantage instead of forcing the upper-handle contact.

decisions.plan: Increase the outward hand tilt in a bounded increment, then resume inward handle contact.
decisions.belief: The hand has backed away and begun tilting outward; the drawer and bowl remain stationary. More tilt is needed to keep the hand body behind the fingertips.
decisions.why: Moves the bulky hand away from the upper handles while retaining fingertip reach.

decisions.plan: Increase tilt a little more while remaining outside contact, then push inward at handle height.
decisions.belief: The outward tilt is progressing freely and clearly moves the hand body away from the cabinet. The bowl remains stationary inside the drawer.
decisions.why: Builds sufficient upper-handle clearance before the remaining closing travel.

decisions.plan: Increase the tilt while moving slightly inward toward the bottom handle, then resume closing pushes.
decisions.belief: The hand now tilts outward by about 20 degrees, improving clearance, and the drawer contents are unchanged.
decisions.why: Maintains fingertip reach while moving the hand body farther away from the upper handles.

decisions.plan: Push inward in a short segment while settling the outward tilt, monitoring for renewed drawer movement.
decisions.belief: The hand is now angled outward and the fingertips are beside the bottom handle. The bowl remains seated inside the partially closed drawer.
decisions.why: Tests whether the tilted approach clears the upper handles during closure.

decisions.plan: Continue positive-y handle pushes with this outward-tilted hand, shortening travel near the final stop.
decisions.belief: The tilted approach has moved the bottom drawer farther inward past the latest stall point. The bowl remains upright and contained.
decisions.why: Reduces the remaining drawer opening while keeping the hand clear of the upper handles.

decisions.plan: Increase outward tilt slightly during a shorter inward push to preserve clearance through the last portion of travel.
decisions.belief: The drawer continued inward but the hand has limited clearance and the opening is still visible. The bowl remains contained and upright.
decisions.why: Keeps the hand body outside the cabinet handles while the fingertips continue the closing slide.

decisions.plan: Apply a final short inward handle push, then withdraw and inspect that the drawer stays shut.
decisions.belief: The bottom drawer is now nearly closed, with only a narrow visible gap; the bowl has moved inside the cabinet with it. The tilted hand remains in closing contact.
decisions.why: Seats the drawer near its end stop without a long overtravel command.

decisions.plan: Leave the cream cheese undisturbed and approach above the butter for a closer alignment check.

decisions.plan: Lift clear of the rim, carry the butter above an adjacent area inside the basket, then inspect before releasing.

decisions.plan: Shift inward, lower only to z=0.595 m, release into the cavity, and withdraw to inspect both objects.

decisions.why: This keeps the butter inside the rim while avoiding another deep-hand insertion and preserving the cream-cheese placement.

decisions.plan: Pick the butter first, verify attachment with a short lift, and place it inside the basket. Then transfer the cream cheese. Approach above the butter with the open gripper.

decisions.plan: Descend around the butter, close the jaws, and lift 5 cm for a visual attachment check.

decisions.why: The short test lift will distinguish a secure grasp from closure beside or above the package.

decisions.plan: Close at the current height and make a short upward test, then inspect whether the butter follows.

decisions.plan: Stop downward motion, open at this interior position, and lift straight up to inspect the placement.
